subtitle: uniform interior C^{1,α} regularity in every dimension d ≥ 3
summary: Bounded infinity-harmonic functions in d ≥ 3 dimensions are C^{1,α_d} in the interior, with a uniform dimensional estimate.
problem: Infinity-harmonic functions are the viscosity solutions of the infinity Laplace equation Δ_∞u = ⟨D²u ∇u, ∇u⟩ = 0, the Euler–Lagrange equation of absolutely minimizing Lipschitz extensions. The OpenAI preprint “Uniform Interior C^{1,α} Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions” (October 4, 2026) proves a uniform interior C^{1,α_d} estimate for bounded infinity-harmonic functions in every dimension d ≥ 3 (Theorem 1.1). We formalize Theorem 1.1 end-to-end using LEAP, with infinity-harmonicity defined in the viscosity sense.
statement: For every integer d ≥ 3 there are constants α_d ∈ (0, 1/3] and C_d < ∞ such that every bounded infinity-harmonic function u ∈ C(B₁), B₁ ⊂ ℝ^d, belongs to C^{1,α_d}(B_{1/2}) and satisfies ‖∇u‖_{L^∞(B_{1/2})} + [∇u]_{C^{0,α_d}(B_{1/2})} ≤ C_d osc_{B₁} u.
title: Uniform Interior C^{1,α} Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions
